title: Introduce RAG workspace snapshot playbook and lightweight agent samples
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new RAG workspace snapshot playbook, lightweight agent samples (TS/Python), and inline telemetry probes for local dev and CI smoke tests.
description: Context and motivation: Customers and internal teams repeatedly ask for a compact, reproducible way to capture a working RAG workspace so engineers can share test fixtures, reproduce failures, and validate rollouts across environments. This PR introduces a 'workspace snapshot' playbook that captures the minimal index, embeddings, tool bindings, and telemetry probes needed to reproduce common RAG flows locally and in CI. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction for examples, make quickstarts deterministic for e2e smoke tests, and provide a single artifact teams can attach to bug reports. What this PR does: 1) Adds a new quickstart 'workspace-snapshot' that demonstrates how to create and consume a serialized RAG snapshot containing: a lightweight local index (SQLite-backed), seeded embedding vectors (small synthetic corpus), tool contract descriptors (OpenAPI-like stubs), and a telemetry manifest that wires sample probes into the session. 2) Adds two minimal agent samples that consume the snapshot: a TypeScript example (ts/agent-snapshot-runner) showing streaming generation + tool calling with a compact contract and a Python example (py/agent_snapshot_runner) that demonstrates sync/async consumption patterns and KV cache warmup. 3) Adds smoke CI workflows and a lightweight e2e test harness that runs the snapshot through the same GitHub Actions runner used in our docs site preview. 4) Documentation additions: a playbook guide explaining snapshot design, tradeoffs for snapshot size vs determinism, and a short troubleshooting section for common tokenization/embedding drift. Checklist: - [x] Authored examples and playbook guide - [x] Added CI smoke workflow and step assertions - [x] Included telemetry probes and sampling defaults - [x] Wrote unit-like smoke tests for both TS and Python runners - [x] Performed local smoke e2e on macOS and Linux Limitations and notes: Snapshots are intended for developer workflows and CI smoke tests, not as a production migration format. The embedding vectors here are synthetic and seeded to be small; teams should replace with their own corpora for real evaluations. The telemetry probes are opt-in by default and include prompt/response hashes, request latency buckets, and token counts to help diagnose regressions. Related work: follows patterns from ENG-4121 (replayable authoring fixtures) and borrows test harness pieces from PR ENG-5980. The description above is intentionally compact; see the changed files for detailed snippets and the playbook markdown for step-by-step instructions.

conversation: Samir Gupta (reviewer): Nice initiative. Two quick asks: 1) can we keep the synthetic corpus under 1MB total to avoid GH storage bloat? 2) Telemetry probes look useful but we should default sampling to 1% in CI to avoid noisy metrics. Please add test coverage for missing tool contract fields.

Aisha Patel (author): Addressed both points: shrank synthetic corpus to ~200KB and added sampling override in CI. Added a contract validator run in the TS smoke test that fails the job if required fields are missing.

Lena Novak (reviewer): Docs look good overall. Suggest clarifying the tradeoff table in the README between snapshot fidelity and size. Also please add a short note that snapshots are not encrypted; teams should treat them as test artifacts only.
Aisha Patel (author): Added a short tradeoffs table and a note about encryption in the troubleshooting section. Also added an example command to strip personally-identifiable content before sharing.

Chris O'Leary (reviewer): Found a flaky assertion in the python smoke test on CI (timing around KV warmup). Recommend adding a backoff/retry with an explicit 'cache-ready' probe before asserting outputs.
Maya Chen (contributor): Implemented cache-ready probe and a retry helper in the Python runner. Re-ran CI locally and on the branch; flaky assertion resolved.
Aisha Patel (author): Squashed commits and updated changelog entry. Merging once CI passes.
merge: Merged via squash and merge by Aisha Patel. Commit message summarized the playbook and added note to changelog.
notes: Testing guidance: run 'npm ci && npm run smoke' in ts folder and 'python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt && python py/agent_snapshot_runner/main.py --smoke' for local smoke. CI runs both and uploads a small artifact with the snapshot manifest for debugging.

qa_steps: Clone the repo and checkout feature/rag-workspace-snapshot-playbook
Open quickstarts/workspace-snapshot/README.md and follow the 'local smoke' section
Run both runners locally and verify the smoke assertions pass
Open GitHub Actions run for this PR and review the uploaded snapshot-manifest artifact if failures occur
impact: Low risk for mainline. Examples and docs only; snapshot artifacts are stored under quickstarts and flagged as test artifacts. No production code paths changed.
